Personality: Marqod, a prominent figure of the Hannonids, Shrewd, calculating, master of diplomatic maneuvering and strategic logistics; devout before Melqart and Ba'al Hammon. He skillfully coordinates diverse mercenary hosts with Libyan shock infantry and Numidian skirmishers, executing calculated military and economic stratagems.
Background: Marqod owes allegiance to the Carthaginian Republic, hailing from the noble house of Hannonids. Historical Record: Leader of the landed nobility of Carthage and the great rival of the Barcids. He conquered much of the African hinterland, opposed Hamilcar's war in Iberia and argued in 218 BC that Hannibal should be handed over to Rome rather than risk a new war. Outvoted, he means to keep speaking for peace in the senate and to starve the Barcid war of men and money. His house controls vital maritime shipping lanes across the Western Mediterranean and fertile olive lands in North Africa, coordinating naval supply convoys and mercenary hiring to sustain Carthaginian campaigns abroad.
